title: The Ice Lets Go
skyStory: The waning gibbous moon, eighty-eight percent lit, stays deep in Scorpio, and down on the coast the shore ice finally lets go. It groans, cracks and drifts out with the tide in great white rafts. Pluto, Scorpio's ruler, watches with approval. Letting go is its favourite sport. The moon pulls the tide a little harder tonight, just to help the last stubborn floes on their way.

reading: Something you have been holding tightly, a plan, an expectation, a way things were supposed to go, is ready to drift out with the tide. You will feel it loosen around midday. Do not grab it back. Watch it float.

The Tiger is a hunter, and hunters hate letting prey go. But today the best catch is the one you release. The [[The Hanged Man]] hangs upside down in your path, perfectly calm, seeing everything from a new angle. Try it. Sit somewhere unusual, a step, the floor, the back seat, and look at your week from there. Something you were forcing will suddenly look optional.
joel.mission: Sit somewhere you never sit, like the floor or a stair, for ten minutes and think about your week from there.
joel.omen: Ice sliding off a roof or drifting on water. It means a stuck situation is about to move freely on its own.

reading: This is a shore day in the biggest sense. The ice is leaving, the water is coming back, and you can hear the waves again for the first time since December. You were born on the longest night, and this is the moment the light you promised fully arrives at the water's edge.

If you can, go stand near open water today, even a creek or a puddle catching sky. Let your mother of pearl catch the light. The [[Six of Swords]] is mid-crossing, and today the boat slides out of the ice and into open water. The rowing gets easier from here. You will feel it in your shoulders by evening, a lightness that is new.
nancy.mission: Visit any open water, even a puddle, and drop one small stone or twig in to mark the crossing.
nancy.omen: The sound of water moving where there was only silence. It means the long crossing has reached easier water.

together.text: Ice-out day. Each of you name one thing from this winter you are leaving on the ice as it drifts away. Say it to each other, one sentence each. Then name one thing you want the open water to bring this spring.
